user_query: I need an object detection model to locate furniture in indoor photographs. It should handle cluttered rooms, partial occlusion, varied lighting, and objects viewed from different angles. Inference will run on CPU-only backend servers with approximately 8 CPU cores and 16 GB of RAM. The model should aim for a mAP@0.5:0.95 of approximately 0.30 or higher, with typical inference latency below 500 milliseconds per image.
use_case_description: Detect furniture in indoor photographs; robust to cluttered rooms, partial occlusion, varied lighting, and objects viewed from different angles.

available_hardware.details: CPU-only inference target; indoor furniture object detection.

model.description: CPU-friendly YOLOv8 detector selected to detect furniture in indoor scenes. Aims to balance accuracy and CPU latency on a 8-core, 16 GB RAM server. Trained or finetuned on furniture examples from openimages_challenge_2019_det_train/val. Uses data augmentation, multi_scale inputs, and non-maximum suppression. Target mAP@0.5:0.95 >= 0.3 with inference latency under 500 ms per image on CPU. Handles clutter, partial occlusion, lighting variation, and multi-angle views by training with occlusion and photometric jitter.

model_selection_decision_evidence.rationale: Rationale for architecture choice: The task requires detecting furniture in indoor scenes with clutter, partial occlusion, varied lighting, and viewing angles, using CPU-only inference on 8 cores with 16 GB RAM and a latency budget under 500 ms per image. Among the available architectures, yolov8 offers the best balance of accuracy and speed for CPU-based deployment in this family, especially when using a smaller variant or optimized CPU backends. RetinaNet R50 FPN and Faster R-CNN variants tend to be heavier on CPU and may struggle to meet the latency target, while SSD300_coco is lighter but typically underperforms on the asked mAP target for a furniture class in indoor scenes. RTDet HGNetv2 L is likely too large for the CPU budget. The chosen model should be trained/finetuned on the furniture subset of Open Images (as provided) with augmentation such as photometric jitter, random occlusion, and multi-scale inputs to improve robustness to clutter, occlusion, lighting, and angle variation. If measured latency on your hardware exceeds 500 ms per image, a practical fallback is SSD300_coco or Faster R-CNN R50 FPN_1x, with input resolution reduced to trade off speed for accuracy. The presence of Open Images furniture data supports learning to distinguish furniture from clutter and occluders in indoor environments. Latency feasibility and exact mAP must be validated on target CPUs; this patch provides a starting point with a CPU-friendly architecture and a clear fallback path.
